correctness.rationale: The source's symmetric-Minkowski-plane lemma applies because the regular dodecagon is invariant under the coordinate symmetries and quarter-turn, so every admissible unit partner is plus or minus Rx. The sign choice gives the same Omega objective. Dihedral reduction leaves one edge parameter a, and edge reflection gives Phi(1-a)=Phi(a). Exact comparison of all six signed facet functionals on 0<=a<=1/2 yields A, C and the two B branches with the sole transition q=(5-2sqrt(3))/13. The two exact derivative formulas are nonnegative/positive on their stated intervals, so the unique reduced maximum is a=1/2. Direct exact substitution gives the claimed chord values and Omega=14/5-sqrt(3).
risks: The published symmetric-plane lemma is a nontrivial structural input; the package independently verifies all hypotheses specific to the regular dodecagon and replays the resulting facet computation.
The result is normalization-independent only under linear isometry; the displayed coordinates use the Euclidean-vertex normalization stated in the claim.

value.rationale: The result is not only an isolated number: it gives the complete reduced Omega profile on a canonical non-Hilbert symmetric polygon, identifies the sole active-facet transition, proves strict monotonicity to the symmetry point, and classifies all maximizers. This supplies an exact benchmark for how a source-defined isosceles-orthogonality invariant interacts with polyhedral facet geometry, information not recoverable from the dodecagon's other known scalar constants.
risks: The computation is specific to the regular dodecagon and does not yet establish a general regular-polygon law.
